messages:
Sophia: Observed sustained queue growth on reserved pool rsv-pool-42 in us-west-2. Admission controller started returning 429s with `reserved_capacity_saturated` at ~06:12 UTC. Customers routing to dedicated are seeing fallback to hosted and increased error rates.
Liam: I'm seeing the same in metrics — queue depth jumped from ~20 to 320 over 7m. CPU+GPU headroom at 0-2%.
Arjun: Logs show admission controller triggered fairshare throttle: `admit=false reason=pool_saturation fairshare=0.3`. Example: `admit_request tenant=acme-corp id=tx-89a status=throttled`.
Priya: Paging playbook: prioritized tenants should get burst override. Do we have an emergency override?
Sophia: We have a temporary `burst_override` flag but it's gated by commit checks. SalesOps, heads-up: this will likely impact some committed tenants.
SalesOps: Confirmed — two customers on commit S1 in that pool. Please add them to incident update.
Olivia: Is there an immediate mitigation that doesn't require infra deploy? Could we lower model sizes for non-critical routes (e.g., switch to 8-bit quant) or route lower-tier tenants to hosted?
Arjun: We can do two quick things: 1) enable temporary reduce-batch-size on the pool to free slots for latency-sensitive calls, 2) toggle `burst_override` for S1 tenants. Both are config flips.
Liam: Reduce-batch-size will increase per-token latency/cost but may reduce queue backlog. Which is lower-risk?
Priya: Triage decision: protect S1 customers first. Enable burst_override for S1, then enable routing fallback for best-effort tenants to hosted.
Sophia: Agreed. Arjun — can you run the override and the route change? Add a revert plan.
Arjun: Running now. Command I'm using: 
```
rb-admin pool-config set rsv-pool-42 --burst-override=enable --override-tenants="acme-corp,zenhealth" --apply
rb-admin routing set --pool rsv-pool-42 --fallback hosted --match-tier best-effort --duration 30m
```
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: pool-config-change rsv-pool-42 by Arjun — job id dpl-4221 — started
Arjun: `burst_override` applied, router rules pushed. I'm seeing admitted requests for the S1 tenants resuming. Queue depth dropping from 320 -> 120 in the last 6m.
Liam: Good. But we're observing a spike in hosted ingress because of the fallback, hosted P99 tokens and cost increased — estimate +28% token spend this hour. Nina / Finance note.
Nina: Noted. Please add a cost tag to the incident. We'll reconcile with SalesOps for committed credits.
Priya: Next: long-term fix — add capacity (scale up reserved pool), or rebalance tenants across AZs. Are there spare GPUs in ap-southeast that can be migrated?
Arjun: Cross-AZ live migration won't be fast. We have unused capacity in eu-west-1 but network egress/latency concerns for these tenants. Scaling pool requires provision lead time ~45m (alloc + setup).
Sophia: Short-term: keep burst_override for S1, routing fallback for best-effort, monitor backlog. Medium: request +2 cards to pool (scale up) and start a scheduled rebalance to even out tenant weights. Long-term: improve autoscaler to pre-warm capacity when queue growth > threshold.
Liam: Opening a provisioning ticket with infra now: INF-7832 — request +2 A100 to rsv-pool-42, priority high.
SalesOps: I'll draft customer comms for the two affected S1 customers: short ETA and mitigation steps.
Sophia: Assigning action items: Arjun — keep watchers on queue + admission metrics and revert if noisy. Liam — validate that TTL on routing fallback is 30m and ready to extend if needed. Priya — coordinate customer updates. Nina — cost tagging.
Arjun: Watchers in place. If queue > 200 after 20m, I'll escalate to scale up automatically.
Liam: Monitor dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/pools/rsv-pool-42 — P99 latency now 320ms, was 210ms before incident.
Priya: Recording incident timeline and linking to ops runbook. Incident doc: INC-2026-0432.
Sophia: Good work. Postmortem follow-ups: 1) tighten admit controller thresholds, 2) add cheaper fallback policy for best-effort that's less hosted-cost heavy, 3) add capacity runbook for faster +2 card provisioning.
Olivia: For future prevention, can Optimize suggest pre-quantization for requests during pool congestion? That could reduce pressure.
Arjun: Noted — will file a feature request with eng-ml.
Sophia: Closing loop — backlog back under 40, burst_override still on, scaling ticket open. Will update again in 30m. :thumbsup:
SalesOps: Sent customer note to S1s, flagged for credit review.
Nina: Cost tag applied.
Sophia: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
summary: Reserved pool rsv-pool-42 in us-west-2 saturated; admission controller throttled new leases causing fallbacks to hosted and cost spike. Immediate mitigation: enabled burst_override for S1 tenants and routing fallback for best-effort tenants; provisioning ticket opened to add GPUs; monitoring continues.
